goal: No export of a production file is kept alive only by a test without a written reason, no test file mocks server-only, the integration tests take next/cache from one setup file, and the scan tests read the source tree through one helper.
why: 443 exports (2,959 lines) in production files are used by tests only, 579 test files mock server-only though the configuration can stub it, 465 integration tests stub next/cache in five spellings, and 84 test files call readdirSync with 67 private walkers. After: testOnlyExports is empty with 100 to 130 reasoned names in keptForTests, 0 files mock server-only, under 60 integration tests stub next/cache themselves, and 20 or fewer test files call readdirSync.

commits.title: Tests take server-only from the configuration, not from a mock in each file

changes.how: In resolve.alias add `"server-only": fileURLToPath(new URL("./test/server-only.ts", import.meta.url))`, the same line vitest.integration.config.mts line 10 has. Nothing else.

Delete, in every test file, the exact line `vi.mock("server-only", () => ({}));` (579 files; all 579 have this one spelling). Do it with one command, not by hand: rg -l 'vi[.]mock[(].server-only' src --glob '*.test.ts' --glob '*.test.tsx' | xargs sed -i '/^vi\.mock("server-only", () => ({}));$/d'. Then, in each file where `vi` is no longer used at all, the linter says so: remove `vi` from that file's vitest import (pnpm lint names each file). Do not delete any other line. If a file has a blank line doubled where the mock was, leave it; the formatter is not part of this step.

commits.title: Integration tests take next/cache from one setup file

changes.how: `import { vi } from "vitest";` and one mock: `vi.mock("next/cache", () => ({ cacheLife: () => {}, cacheTag: () => {}, updateTag: () => {}, revalidateTag: () => {}, revalidatePath: () => {}, refresh: () => {} }));` (these six are every name production code imports from next/cache: rg -o 'import [{]([^}]*)[}] from "next/cache"' src --glob '!*.test.ts'; add a name that rg shows and this list lacks). A header comment says: a test file's own vi.mock("next/cache") still wins for that file, so a test that records tags keeps its own. Do not mock next/headers or next/server here in this commit.

Add `setupFiles: ["./test/integration-mocks.ts"],` to `test`. Before deleting anything, prove the override on one file: run a test that has its own multi-line next/cache mock with a spy (rg -l 'vi[.]mock[(]"next/cache", [(][)] => [(][{]$' src --glob '*.int.test.ts' lists 40) and see it still pass.

Delete the one-line next/cache mocks whose body is only no-ops, one spelling per run of the command, each followed by pnpm test:int: (1) 318 files: `vi.mock("next/cache", () => ({ cacheLife: () => {}, cacheTag: () => {}, updateTag: () => {}, revalidateTag: () => {}, refresh: () => {} }));` (2) 39 files without refresh, (3) 25 without revalidateTag, (4) 24 with only cacheLife, cacheTag and updateTag, (5) 15 with refresh before revalidateTag, (6) 2 with `() => undefined`. Get the exact lines with: rg -o --no-filename 'vi[.]mock[(]"next/cache", .*' src --glob '*.int.test.ts' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn. Delete a line only when every value in it is `() => {}` or `() => undefined`. Keep the 40 multi-line mocks and any one-line mock that records something (one pushes tags into an array). Then remove unused `vi` imports as pnpm lint names them.

commits.title: One walker for the tests that read the source tree

changes.how: Test support, never imported by production code. `import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs"; import { join, relative } from "node:path";`. Export `ROOT` (the repository root: join(__dirname, "../..")), `sourceFiles(dir: string, options?: { tests?: boolean; extensions?: readonly string[]; skip?: (rel: string) => boolean }): string[]`: repository-relative posix paths of every file under `dir`, recursive, sorted, never entering node_modules, .next or .git; by default only .ts and .tsx and no *.test.ts, *.test.tsx or *.spec.ts (tests: true includes them). Export `sourceText(rel: string): string`. Both keep a module-level Map memo (the list per dir-and-options key, the text per file), so one worker walks and reads a file once. Export `actionFiles()`: the files whose first statement is 'use server'. This file holds the only readdirSync the scans need.

Tests: sourceFiles("src/lib") contains src/lib/money.ts and no *.test.ts; with tests: true it contains src/lib/money.test.ts; it lists more than 500 files for "src"; a second call returns the same array object (the memo); sourceText returns a string that contains `export` for src/lib/money.ts.

List the files: rg -l readdirSync src --glob '*.test.ts' (84 on 12 November 2026; step 3.15's and 1.17's new scans may add some). In each, find the private walker (a recursive function that calls readdirSync and statSync and filters by extension) and replace it by sourceFiles() with the SAME folder and the SAME filter: pass what the walker left out as `skip`, and keep any extra filter the test applied after the walk. Replace readFileSync(join(ROOT, file)) by sourceText(file) where the path is one sourceFiles() returned. Delete the walker and the unused imports. Do them in this order and commit every ten files: first the 46 named *.scan.test.ts, then the others. For each file, before and after: add a temporary console.log of the number of files the test walks and see the same number; remove the log. Leave a test alone (and count it in the 20 allowed) when it reads a folder that is not source code: supabase/migrations, content/docs, public, e2e fixtures, a temporary directory it made itself. Also in this commit, two lines the finding names: in src/lib/brand.scan.test.ts, in oldNames() right after the file's text is read (about line 33), add `if (!OLD.some((re) => re.test(src))) return [];` before ts.createSourceFile (use the variable name the text has there); the same in oldWords() of src/lib/theme-words.scan.test.ts (about line 49).

commits.title: Exports only a test keeps alive: delete, or keep with a reason, folder by folder

changes.how: The list is `testOnlyExports` in src/server/unused.baseline.json (entries 'file#name'; print it grouped by folder: node -e "const b=require('./src/server/unused.baseline.json');for(const e of b.testOnlyExports)console.log(e)" | sort). Work one folder per commit: src/lib first (about 260 names), then src/server, then src/components. For each name N in file F: (a) run rg -w -l N src e2e --glob '*.test.*' --glob '*.spec.*' to get the tests that name it, and read F's comment above N. (b) KEEP, by moving the entry to keptForTests with a one-sentence reason (node scripts/unused.mjs --write, then replace its TODO), when one of these is true: the comment says a test holds a rule with it; it is a reset or clean-up helper (closeDb, a forget or reset function); it is an oracle a test compares the real result against (buildInvoiceSnapshot, buildEditInvoiceSnapshot, creditNoteSnapshot, editCreditNote, nextState, validateExport, the two registerProblems); it is a constant a guard test reads (STORE_MATCHER, SECRET_TABLES, NOT_EXPORTED). (c) MOVE to a `*-test-support.ts` file beside F when it is a pure helper only tests call and it uses nothing private of F. (d) If the comment names a screen or a caller that does not call it (openRequestCount 'the Requests tab's badge', trialPausedAt 'for the banner', twoStepMembers, retryDocumentPdf, shopperCanAccessOrder 'for the order page and My account'): do not delete; write the name, the file and the comment's claim into a list for the owner in your report (a missing wire is not waste), and give it the keptForTests reason 'named by a screen that does not call it: owner to decide, listed <date>'. (e) Otherwise DELETE the export (the whole function or constant, or only the `export` keyword when the file itself uses it) and the test cases that only exercise it; when a test file is then empty, delete the file. If a deleted test case was the only check of a database rule reached through the function (a trigger, a constraint), keep the case and reach the rule through the function the app uses. After each folder: pnpm lint (it names what became unused in turn; delete those too), node scripts/ratchet.mjs, node scripts/unused.mjs --write.

The same for src/server and then src/components. Two named switches of test set-up to the function the app uses, then delete the old one: setCartCode to addCartCode in src/server/checkout-kinds.int.test.ts, vat-engine.int.test.ts and vat-money-review.int.test.ts; listOrders to listOrdersPage in src/server/fulfilment.int.test.ts, inventory-admin.int.test.ts and store-copy.int.test.ts (these six files are the only tests whose set-up lines may change; their assertions may not). SCOPES_BEFORE_D440 in src/lib/admin-api.ts line 68 and the case in src/lib/admin-api-routes.test.ts lines 196 to 211 go together. chosenDelivery: after deleting it, correct the sentence in the header of src/server/delivery-readers.scan.test.ts line 8, which says cartSummary() and placeOrder() call it (they call resolveDelivery()). After each deletion that a rule names: rg -w N docs/rules CLAUDE.md and correct the sentence.

do_not: Do not delete an export that any non-test file imports: the list comes from scripts/unused.mjs, and pnpm typecheck must pass after every folder.
Do not delete an oracle, a reset helper or a guard list because only tests read it: those go to keptForTests.
Do not delete a function whose comment names a screen that should call it; list it for the owner.
Do not change a test's assertion. Deleted with its export: yes. Rewritten to pass: no (the six named set-up switches aside).
Do not mock next/headers or next/server in the shared setup in this step, and do not delete a multi-line or recording mock.
Do not move a scan's ban into the shared walker's defaults: each scan keeps its own filter.
Do not add a bypass to the app for a test; these are test-side stubs only.
Do not sweep makeStore and paidOrder helpers: they stay 'when touched'.
stop_if: A test fails after its server-only or next/cache line was deleted: restore that file's line, name the file and go on with the others; stop if more than ten files need it.
A scan walks a different number of files after moving to sourceFiles().
scripts/unused.mjs or src/server/unused.baseline.json does not exist (step 1.17 is not done).
Deleting an export breaks a non-test file's build (the scan missed an import form): stop and report the import.
More than 30 exports fall under rule (d) (a comment that names a caller that does not call it): report the list before deleting further.
executor_why: The first three commits are mechanical and a cheap model can do them with the commands given, but deciding for about 330 exports whether each is an oracle, a seam, a missing wire or dead code is judgement per item.
